title: Developing 3D Organized Human Cardiac Tissue within a Microfluidic Platform
protocol: Clean a silicon wafer with isopropyl alcohol and dry with nitrogen.
Bake the wafer at 200 °C for 5 min.
Deposit 3-4 mL of SU8 in the center of the wafer, then spin to form a layer of 200 μm.
Soft bake the wafer for 7 min at 65 °C and then 45 min at 95 °C.
Place the transparent mask with the UV filter into the mask holder.
Expose the wafer to 2 cycles of 230 mJ/cm², with a 30 s delay between exposures.
Perform a post-exposure bake on the exposed wafer in a 50 °C oven overnight.
Turn off the oven the next morning.
Submerge the cooled wafer in SU8-developer after it reaches room temperature.
Remove the wafer from the developer every 5 min and wash with IPA, then place it back in the developer.
Dry the wafer with air nitrogen after around 20 min or when the IPA runs clear.
Hard bake the wafer in an oven set to 150 °C without opening the oven until it reaches room temperature.
Confirm the height of SU8 with a profilometer and the optical features with a light microscope.
Tape the wafer inside a 150 mm plastic Petri dish.
Invert the wafer over a glass Petri dish containing 0.4 mL of methyltrichlorosilane (MTCS) for 4 min.
Place the lid on the Petri dish after turning the wafer upright.
Mix 30 g of silicone elastomer base to the curing agent at a 10:1 ratio.
Pour the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) on the wafer and degas within a desiccator.
Cure the PDMS by placing the wafer at 80 °C for 1.5 h.
Carefully peel off the PDMS.
Punch inlets and outlets for tissue ports with a 1 mm biopsy punch.
Punch inlets and outlets for media channels with a 1.5 mm biopsy punch.
Clean the PDMS channels with tape to remove dust.
Soak coverslips (18 x 18 mm, No.1) in 70% ethanol for at least 15 min.
Dry the coverslips off with tissue wipes.
Expose both coverslips and PDMS channels to plasma setting on high for 1 min.
Quickly bond together the coverslips and PDMS channels.
Place bonded devices in an 80 °C oven overnight to secure the bond.
Apply mild pressure on the edges of PDMS channels during bonding to ensure a good seal between PDMS and glass.
Submerge the bonded PDMS devices in deionized water (DI H2O).
Autoclave the devices with the liquid cycle.
Aspirate the liquid from the devices after autoclaving.
Autoclave the devices again with the gravity cycle.
Dehydrate the sterilized devices overnight at 80 °C.
Thaw one aliquot of the matrix medium on ice by adding it to 25 mL of DMEM/F-12K.
Dispense 1 mL of this suspension into each well of a 6-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for at least 1 hour.
Modify E8 media by adding 5 µM of Y-27632 to use for hiPSC culture for 24 h after thawing.
Change media to fresh E8 after 24 hours.
Passage cells at Day 3 or Day 4 when they are around 70% confluent.
Aspirate media and wash each well with 1 mL of DPBS.
Add 1 mL of 0.5 mM EDTA to each well and incubate at room temperature for 6-7 minutes.
Carefully aspirate EDTA, then add 1 mL of E8+RI into each well.
Blast against the surface with a pipette (~5-10 times) to collect all cells.
Collect the cell suspension in a microcentrifuge tube and count the cells.
Passage at desired cell density (i.e., ~200 K per well) in E8+RI.
Change media to E8 without RI 24 hours after passage.
Prepare RPMI + B27 - insulin by adding 10 mL of B27 minus insulin and 5 mL of penicillin/streptomycin (pen/strep) to 500 mL of RPMI 1640.
Prepare RPMI + B27 + insulin by adding 10 mL of B27 and 5 mL of pen/strep to 500 mL of RPMI 1640.
Prepare RPMI minus glucose + B27 + insulin by adding 10 mL of B27, 5 mL of pen/strep, and 4 mM sodium lactate to 500 mL of RPMI 1640 without glucose.
Replace the old medium with 4 mL of the RPMI + B27 - insulin medium containing 10 µM CHIR99021 when hiPSCs reach 85% confluency.
Aspirate the medium exactly 24 hours later (Day 1).
Replace with 5 mL of prewarmed RPMI + B27 - insulin to each well.
Collect 2.5 mL of spent medium from each well exactly 72 hours after CHIR99021 addition (Day 3).
Add 15 mL of fresh RPMI + B27 - insulin medium to the collected spent medium.
Add IWP2 to a concentration of 5 µM to the combined medium tube.
Remove approximately 1.5 mL of remaining medium per well so that 1 mL remains.
Swirl the plate vigorously to ensure adequate removal of cell debris.
Aspirate the rest of the old medium and add 5 mL of combined medium containing IWP2 per well.
On Day 5, aspirate the medium from each well.
Replace with 5 mL of prewarmed RPMI + B27 - insulin.
On Day 7, aspirate the medium from each well.
Replace with 5 mL of prewarmed RPMI + B27 + insulin.
On Day 9, aspirate the medium from each well.
Replace with 5 mL of prewarmed RPMI + B27 + insulin.
On Day 11, aspirate the medium from each well.
Replace with 5 mL of prewarmed RPMI + B27 + insulin.
On Day 13, start glucose starvation by aspirating the medium from each well.
Wash each well with 1 mL of 1x DPBS.
Add 5 mL of prewarmed RPMI minus glucose + B27 + insulin supplemented with 4 mM sodium lactate per well.
On Day 16, repeat glucose starvation procedure as on Day 13.
Aspirate the spent medium from each well on Day 19.
Replace it with 5 mL of prewarmed RPMI + B27 + insulin in each well for cell recovery after purification.
Replate cells following the CM dissociation protocol (step 3.3) on Day 21, aiming to plate 1.5-2 x 10^6 cells per well in a 6-well plate.
Aspirate the medium from each well and replace it with 4 mL of RPMI + B27 + insulin every 2-3 days starting from Day 21.
Culture human ventricular cardiac fibroblasts (hCFs) in T75 flasks at a density of 250K cells per flask using Fibroblast Growth Media-3 (FGM3).
Change the media every other day for hCF culture.
Passage hCFs when they reach 70% confluence, using cells before passage 10 to avoid differentiation to myofibroblasts.
Begin aspirating the spent media from the flask during hCF dissociation.
Wash the T75 flask with 3 mL of 1x DPBS.
Aspirate the DPBS from the flask.
Take 3 mL of prewarmed 1x Trypsin-EDTA (0.05%) and add it to the flask.
Tilt the flask and swirl to coat the bottom.
Incubate the flask in a 37 °C incubator for 4-6 min.
Check the cells under a microscope for detachment, evidenced by round cell shape and floating cells.
If necessary, return the flask to the incubator for another minute.
Add 3 mL of prewarmed FGM3 to neutralize trypsin action.
Pipette the solution up and down against the bottom of the flask to dislodge the CFs.
Collect the cell suspension in a 15 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Take 10 µL of the cell suspension and dispense it in a hemocytometer for cell counting with a microscope.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 x g for 4 min.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in fresh FGM3 to make a desired concentration of 75 x 106 cells/mL.
Wash the wells with 1 mL of 1x DPBS per well of a 6-well plate.
Take 6 mL of DPBS and pipette 1 mL per well.
Aspirate DPBS carefully without disturbing attached cells.
Pipette 6 mL of warm cell detachment solution (e.g., TrypLE express) and add 1 mL per well.
Incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Neutralize the enzyme with an equal volume of RPMI + B27+ insulin.
Mechanically dissociate cells by pipetting up and down against the culture vessel with a 1 mL pipette.
Collect cells in a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 3 min.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 5 mL of RPMI + B27 + insulin.
Pipette solution up and down with a 1 mL pipette to ensure proper mixing.
Take 10 µL of the cell suspension and dispense it in a hemocytometer to determine total cell number.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 3 min to ensure complete removal of TrypLE.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add an appropriate volume of RPMI + B27 + insulin to achieve 75 x 10^6 cells/mL.

If cardiac differentiation/selection does not result in high CM% (i.e., >80%), as evidenced through immunostaining or flow cytometry for CM-specific proteins like cTnT, do not consider cells as suitable for the tissue formation.
Optimize the differentiation process via adjustment of CHIR99021 concentrations and initial starting density if necessary.
Utilize other methods such as fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) or magnetic-activated cell sorting (MACS) to improve CM purification if needed.
Prepare collagen from the high concentration of collagen stock ranging from 8-11 mg/mL.
The final collagen concentration for creating the cell:hydrogel mixture is 2 mg/mL.
Keep all required reagents on ice inside a biosafety hood.
Take 75 µL of stock collagen (8 mg/mL) and dispense it in a microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Slowly aspirate the viscous collagen solution with a pipette.
Take 13.85 μL of media (RPMI + B27 + insulin) and dispense it in the same tube.
Add 10 μL of phenol red to the mixture and resuspend.
Add 1.15 μL of 1N NaOH to the suspension.
Resuspend the suspension using a 200 µL pipette tip.
Mix suspended CMs with CFs at a 4:1 ratio.
Take an aliquot of 8 μL of CMs and add to a fresh centrifuge tube on ice.
Add 2 μL of CFs to the cell suspension in the centrifuge tube.
Resuspend the cell suspension.
Grab 5.6 μL of the cell suspension and put it in a fresh microcentrifuge tube.
Take 4 μL of collagen from previous steps.
Add to a 4:1 CM:CF mixture.
Add 2.4 μL of Growth Factor Reduced (GFR) basement membrane matrix.
Mix up and down to ensure homogenous cell suspension.
Place autoclaved microfluidic devices in Biosafety Cabinet for at least 1 hour before insertion.
Fill a 150 x 15 mm Petri dish with DI H2O to hold 3 of the 60 x 15 mm Petri dishes containing devices.
Resuspend cell:hydrogel mixture thoroughly by pipetting while tube remains on ice.
Insert tip into injection port of microfluidic device.
Inject 3 μL of cell:hydrogel suspension into tissue region inlet using a 20 μL pipette tip.
Remove the tip once the port is filled.
Repeat for all devices or entirety of prepared hydrogel suspension.
Keep the cell:hydrogel suspension on ice for as long as possible.
Insert the solution into devices quickly, pipetting off ice and avoiding polymerization in the tip.
Make small volumes of the cell:hydrogel suspension fresh for each set of 4 devices if many are to be injected.
Flip devices within their Petri dishes with tweezers and place them inside a large Petri dish filled with water.
Incubate at 37°C for 9 minutes for hydrogel polymerization.
Take devices out of the incubator, flip upright, and continue incubation at 37°C for 9 more minutes.
Inject RPMI + B27 + insulin into flanking media channels (~20 μL per device).
Place devices back in the incubator at 37°C.
Change media within the media channels daily with fresh RPMI + B27 + insulin.
Maintain devices within a large Petri dish filled with DI H2O to prevent evaporation of media.
Pipette small droplets of excess RPMI + B27 + insulin on top of channel inlets/outlets during routine media changes.
Place devices in an environmentally-controlled stage incubator.
Record 30 s videos of multiple spots within each device at the maximal frame rate.
Change media in devices in the cell culture hood.
Place back changed devices in cell culture incubator.
Prepare PBS-Glycine by dissolving 100 mM glycine in PBS and adding 0.02% NaN3.
Adjust pH of PBS-Glycine to 7.4 for long-term storage.
Prepare PBS-Tween-20 by adding 0.05% Tween-20 to PBS and adding 0.02% NaN3.
Adjust pH of PBS-Tween-20 to 7.4 for long-term storage.
Prepare IF buffer by adding 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% BSA, and 0.05% Tween-20 to PBS, then add 0.02% NaN3.
Adjust pH of IF buffer to 7.4 for long-term storage.
Resuspend lyophilized goat serum in 2 mL of PBS to make 100% goat serum.
Dilute the 2 mL with 18 mL of PBS to make 10% goat serum.
Fix samples by adding 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) to tissue channels and incubating at 37 °C for 20 min.
Wash cells by adding PBS-Glycine to tissue channels twice for 10 min each at room temperature.
Wash cells by adding PBS-Tween-20 for 10 min at room temperature.
Permeabilize the cells by adding IF buffer to the tissue channels for 30 min at room temperature.
Block the cells by adding a 10% goat serum solution to the tissue channels for 1 h at room temperature.
Dilute non-conjugated primary antibodies in a 10% goat serum solution at desired concentrations, then add to the tissue channels and incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the samples by adding PBS-Tween-20 to tissue channels three times for 20 min each at room temperature.
Dilute secondary antibodies in PBS-Tween-20 at desired concentrations, centrifuge at 10,000 x g for 10 min, then add to the tissue channels.
Incubate samples with secondary antibodies for 30 min to 1 h.
Wash the samples with PBS-Tween-20 three times for 10 min each at room temperature.
Add anti-fade or desired mounting medium to the tissue channels.
Image the samples using fluorescence microscopy or a confocal microscope if higher magnification is needed.
Stack and reconstruct images from different z-planes to form representative 3D images.
